after_the_first_failure.first_verdict_stands: The first test failed its limit, and the second and third measures below do not change that.
after_the_first_failure.cause: The surrogate max(-A r, -A clip(r)) has a gradient that jumps where a sample's ratio crosses 1 +/- clip_param. Rounding moves a few samples across, each one moves the mean gradient by up to about 1 percent, and Adam carries it on. Evidence: on seeds 1 to 3 the KL schedule takes the same branches in every run, so it is not the cause. With clip_param 1000, seed 1 with a fixed schedule falls from 3.3e-2 to 2.2e-5. The step-by-step trace shows the gradient error jump from 2.6e-6 to 7.3e-3 at one mini-batch. The counts of samples that cross were not recorded, so a single crossing is inferred from the size of the jump, not counted.

second_measure.note: Limits written in commit b420bfd before the run on seeds 11 to 20. One seed was run first to see the time, and it is the first of the ten. Passes: no_kink and lockstep, with all faults caught. Fails: free_running, against a control of relative noise in each gradient, which turned out to be the wrong size, and the surrogate loss over 1e-3 on 3 of 10 seeds.

third_measure.note: Limits written in commits 902e3bd and 4ff77e8 before any run on seeds 21 to 30. The control is rsl_rl's own update on MPS against rsl_rl's own on the CPU, and it is valid: it agrees where nothing crosses. MLX's worst actor error is inside 3 times the control's worst, but its median is not inside 3 times the control's median: 9.8e-3 against 2.2e-4. MLX has a large error on 7 of 10 seeds, and the control on 4 of 10. Ten seeds cannot say whether that difference is real.

after_the_first_failure.gate: Open. What this does show: with nothing able to cross the clip, MLX matches rsl_rl to 1.7e-4 at worst against the first limit of 1e-2 on 10 new seeds, and the clipped gradient matches on rsl_rl's own weights to 8.2e-3 at worst. Each injected fault was caught. No free-running measure passed.

after_the_fixes_2026_11_04.summary: The per-op comparison found real defects of the port, and they are fixed. The first and third tests still fail when run again, and those failures stay. A fourth measure, written first on 120 new seeds, passes: MLX lands as far from rsl_rl on the CPU as rsl_rl on MPS does. It does not show that one seed gives the same weights.

defects_found.elu: mx.expm1 on this GPU is biased on negative inputs: mean -11 ulp, max 35 ulp. torch writes exp(x) - 1, and the port now does.
defects_found.log_2pi: mx.log(2 pi) on this GPU is 1 ulp off, 12 times per sample. The constant is now a Python double as in torch.distributions.Normal. Entropy was off by 1.9e-6 on the GPU.
defects_found.power: x**2 in MLX is not correctly rounded (exact on 65 percent on the GPU, 84 percent on the CPU). torch's is, on both of its devices. The port now multiplies.
defects_found.sum_order: mx.sum adds from left to right. torch adds four lanes and then the lanes, on its CPU and on MPS (equal on 2^18 rows of 12 elements). Half of the log probabilities differed by an ulp.
defects_found.gradient_at_a_tie: At a ratio exactly on a clip bound, mx.maximum and mx.clip gave a zero gradient, and torch 2.11 gives the full one. It starts a divergence: on seed 21 at step 3, the first such tie in the run. Torch 2.15's clamp gives 0 at a bound, so this depends on the torch version.

after_the_fixes_2026_11_04.not_defects: The formula, the KL branches, Adam's epsilon and the order of the gradient clip match rsl_rl 5.5.1. Rounding order in the KL, the norm and Adam now follows torch too.

fifth_measure_float64_2026_11_04.rule_changed_after_development_seed_1: No limit changed, and no counted seed had run. As first written, rule 6 held the two clip faults on the actor at max_grad_norm 1.0. That could not pass, because the actor gradient norm stays under 1.0 on this data, so at that setting the clip touches only the critic. Rules 6 and 8 now add max_grad_norm 0.01, where the clip touches the actor. The epsilon fault moved to that setting too, because its critic error at 1.0 was 5.4e-8, under the margin of rule 5.
